page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.6xlarge is a high-capacity storage-oriented instance type within the ecs.d1 server family. Powered by KVM virtualization, it features 24 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The system provides 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

A defining feature of the ecs.d1.6xlarge instance is its bundled local storage array, providing 70,866 GB of hard disk drive (HDD) capacity directly attached to the host. The instance incorporates an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth for interconnectivity and data transfer. It does not include dedicated GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The inclusion of 70,866 GB of local HDD storage alongside 24 dedicated vCPUs makes this instance profile cost-efficient for heavy data storage and batch processing tasks where high capacity takes precedence over flash-based storage performance. The balanced 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio supports memory requirements for big data processing, data logging, distributed file systems, and large-scale data warehousing workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.6xlarge is a dedicated cloud server instance designed for high-density storage applications. Built on KVM virtualization, it incorporates 24 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor operating at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server is configured with 96.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside an 8 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance features a bundled local storage capacity of 70,866 GB delivered via local hard disk drives (HDDs), offering substantial local volume space without requiring external block storage. With zero dedicated GPUs and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses included, the instance trades off flash-based disk speeds for massive local capacity density. This profile provides qualitative resource efficiency for data-intensive processing, distributed file storage, log aggregation, and large database operations requiring high local storage volume.
